sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ramesh Kumar Pandey,Salman Ahmad,Saqib Meezan,Sunil Vashisth
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Salman Ahmad, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 547 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kavi Nagar, District Ghaziabad during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased on 08.11.2019 and deceased worked as A.N.M. and due to her salary applicant and his family members tortured her and on 17.04.2021 after receiving the information when informant arrived at her matrimonial home then found that the room of the deceased was locked and applicant and his family members did not inform the police and after breaking the door he found that deceased was lying dead.

It is further mentioned in Ankur Kumar @ Vishnu Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39425974/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the FIR that on the abdomen of the deceased there was burn marks.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that deceased was pregnant.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and only being husband, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.

He further submits that there is no specific demand of dowry in the FIR but during investigation when the statement of witnesses were recorded then they started making allegation of demand of demand of dowry of a car and this fact clearly suggests that subsequently on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry applicant has been made accused in the present matter.

5. He further submits that even from the FIR it reflects that after breaking the door it was found that deceased was lying dead and this fact clearly suggests that accidentally while doing press on the clothes deceased died due to burn injuries as she sustained burn injuries from the press.
6. He further submits that applicant in the present matter is in jail since 17.05.2021 i.e. for more than two years.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there is specific allegation of demand of dowry of a car in the statements of prosecution witnesses, therefore,
considering the provisions of Section 304B IPC and Section 113B of Indian Evidence Act, applicant should not be released on bail.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Although, applicant is in jail since May, 2021 i.e. for more than two years but he is husband of the deceased and his wife died under abnormal circumstances due to burn injuries in her matrimonial home and defence taken by the applicant does not appear to be convincing.

10. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected.

12. However, considering the fact that applicant is in jail for more than two years, trial court is directed to conclude the trial of the case within eight months from the date of production of certified copy of this order in accordance with law.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 15.9.2023 AK Pandey  Ankur Kumar @ Vishnu Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39425974/
